problem: The business-income summary says business-asset gains without the depreciable-asset exclusion; the debt-satisfaction limb in the grouped ledger is also absent from this step. The next step deals with pool balancing, so the first phrase can invite counting a depreciable disposal gain as well as its balancing inclusion.
quote: gains on the disposal of business assets (other than depreciable assets) or on the satisfaction of business debts
repair: Replace the opening of the s.24 list with: gains on disposal of business assets other than depreciable assets, gains on satisfaction of business debts, s.39(8) pool-balancing inclusions, ... . Keep the existing baseline/currentness qualification.

problem: The ownership-change condition names new business but omits new investment, which is an independent limb of the cited restriction. An investment without a new trade must still enter this baseline check.
quote: does not engage in a new business or investment except with the approval of the Commissioner
repair: State that the company must continue the same business and must not engage in a new business or investment without Commissioner approval for three years after the change. Preserve the stale-cross-reference warning and currentness hold.

problem: The estimate/revision dates are stated as 31 January, 30 April and 31 October without the substituted-year alternatives in s.113(1)-(2). The paragraph does include substituted instalment dates, making the omitted estimate alternatives especially easy to miss.
quote: for a taxpayer using a substituted year of assessment, on or before the end of the first month
additional_quotes: on or before the end of the fourth month
on or before the tenth month
repair: Qualify the three calendar dates as the ordinary-year baseline, then give initial estimate by end of substituted month 1, review by end of month 4, and the source's exact wording for the second review: on or before the tenth month. Do not silently turn the unusual tenth-month wording into an independently confirmed month-end deadline.

problem: The operative aggregation instruction says the foreign branch without stating that s.90(4) limits it to a foreign branch of a resident company. A resident individual with a foreign branch must not infer the same pooling permission.
quote: foreign-source income derived by a foreign branch of a resident company is aggregated and considered a single receipt of income
repair: Use: aggregate foreign-source receipts derived by a foreign branch of a resident company only under s.90(4). Add the resident-company condition to the grouped ledger record and any table wording purporting to state that exception. The example already expressly excludes aggregation and its arithmetic remains correct.
